key_insight: Generalization in quantum policies and value functions is governed more by entanglement-driven Fisher effective dimension than by raw parameter count.
engineering_relevance: For quantum reinforcement learning, entangling connectivity should be treated as a controllable complexity knob because it can worsen train-test generalization even when parameter count is fixed.
method: PAC-Bayesian analysis using Fisher geometry to define effective dimension
Controlled circuit experiments with fixed rotation count and varying entanglement
Evaluation across supervised classification, contextual bandits, value functions, and hardware noise
evidence_signal: Across multiple tasks, circuits with higher Fisher effective dimension showed larger train-test gaps, and the effect persisted on an IBM Heron processor.
watch_item: The strongest ordering results appear in low-variance decision models, while multi-step policy learning remains harder to fully disentangle because return variance is high.
paper_title: Entanglement as a Structural Complexity Axis: A PAC-Bayesian View of Generalization in Quantum Policies and Value Functions
